  1                     REBUTTAL TESTIMONY OF CASEY D. PETTY, P.E.

 2                     I.   INTRODUCTION AND PURPOSE OF TESTIMONY

 3   Q.   ARE YOU THE SAME CASEY D. PETTY, P.E. THAT SUBMITTED DIRECT

 4        TESTIMONY ON BEHALF OF ONCOR ELECTRIC DELIVERY COMPANY LLC

 5        (“ONCOR”) AND LCRA TRANSMISSION SERVICES CORPORATION (“LCRA

 6        TSC” AND TOGETHER, “APPLICANTS”) IN THIS DOCKET?

 7   A.   Yes.

 8   Q.   WHAT IS THE PURPOSE OF YOUR REBUTTAL TESTIMONY?

 9   A.   The purpose of my rebuttal testimony is to address certain claims and issues

10        raised in intervenor direct testimony regarding Oncor and LCRA TSC’s proposed

11        Bell County East Switch to Big Hill Substation 765 kilovolt (“kV”) transmission line

12        project (“Proposed Transmission Line Project” or “Project”). Specifically, I provide

13        testimony of my continued support of Route 894 as the route that best meets the

14        Public Utility Commission of Texas (“Commission”) routing factors while also

15        supporting the selection of any proposed alternative route or any combination of

16        forward-progressing alternative transmission route links that Applicants proposed

17        in this proceeding. Additionally, I address concerns from intervenors about the

18        public participation process, notice, general routing decisions, and impacts related

19        to the Proposed Transmission Line Project.

20   Q.   IF YOU DO NOT ADDRESS A SPECIFIC CLAIM OR INTERVENOR’S

21        TESTIMONY IN YOUR REBUTTAL TESTIMONY, DOES THAT INDICATE THAT

22        YOU AGREE WITH OR CONCEDE THE ISSUES THEY RAISED?



     SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349                                         Petty – Rebuttal
     PUC Docket No. 59475                                             Oncor & LCRA TSC
                                                           Bell County East – Big Hill CCN
                                              -2-
  1   A.     No. Hundreds of pieces of testimony were filed in this docket, many of which raised

 2          substantially the same issues. Therefore, my rebuttal testimony addresses the

 3          issues raised in intervenor testimony without listing each individual party who

 4          raised them. While I frequently cite specific intervenor testimonies, that does not

 5          indicate that my response only applies to that party’s concern or that it does not

 6          apply equally to similar issues voiced by other parties. Moreover, if I fail to address

 7          an issue raised by an intervenor in testimony, it should not be assumed that I agree

 8          with that individual’s testimony.

 9                           I.    REBUTTAL REGARDING ROUTE SELECTION

10   Q.     APPLICANTS IDENTIFIED ROUTE 894 AS THE ROUTE THAT BEST MEETS

11          COMMISSION ROUTING FACTORS IN THE APPLICATION.                                DO OTHER

15          Daniel and Kathryn Voss, and D & M Davis Land and Cattle, LP; Chris Rowntree

16          on behalf of U3 Landowners; 1 Brian C. Andrews on behalf of Glenn and Ryan

17          Hodge, JT Carothers Holdings LLC, MCP 18 LLC, and Schwertner Farms, Inc.;

18          Mark D. Anderson on behalf of Ben E. Keith Company and Jan Yates

19          Boultinghouse Family Trust; and Jason E. Buntz on behalf of the Colorado River

     Williams, Larry Williams, John and Karen Sloan, Pepper Isom, George & Barbara Ellington, Leah Snell,

     Kathy Hughes, Oliver 2012 Limited Family Partnership, Judith Ann McGhee, Rex Oliver, Ross Oliver,
     Robert Oliver, 2BHL, LLC, Paul Rowntree, Clayton Thompson, Floyd Shahan, James & Kimberly Burkett,
     Jake Burnett
     SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349                                                Petty – Rebuttal
     PUC Docket No. 59475                                                    Oncor & LCRA TSC
                                                                  Bell County East – Big Hill CCN
                                                    -3-
  1        Alliance Intervenors; among many others. Other parties, including Commission

 2        Staff (“Staff”), do not agree with Applicants’ selection. Staff identified Route 487

 3        as the best meets route.

 4   Q.   DO APPLICANTS OPPOSE STAFF’S RECOMMENDATION OF ROUTE 487?

 5   A.   Applicants do not oppose the selection of any filed route, including Route 487. As

 6        stated on page 12, lines 16-18 of my direct testimony, each of the routes in

 7        Applicants’ CCN application complies with the Public Utility Regulatory Act

 8        (“PURA”) § 37.056(c)(4)(A)-(D) and 16 Texas Administrative Code (“TAC”) §

 9        25.101(b)(3)(B), including the Commission’s policy of prudent avoidance.

10        Additionally, Applicants have judged all filed routes to be feasible from an

11        engineering perspective based on known constraints.

12   Q.   BASED ON INTERVENOR TESTIMONY, IS THERE AN ALTERNATIVE

13        TRANSMISSION        LINE     ROUTE        THAT   IS    UNOPPOSED         BY    ALL

14        INTERVENORS?

15   A.   No. Every alternative route is opposed by at least one intervenor.

16   Q.   PLEASE DESCRIBE INTERVENOR CONCERNS THAT RELATE TO ROUTE

17        894.

18   A.   Much of the opposition to Route 894 focuses on issues like impacts to recreational

19        enjoyment, wildlife, and hunting land; impacts to cattle grazing and livestock

20        operations; aesthetic and visual impacts; historical and cultural resources impacts

21        related to Native American artifacts; among similar issues. Each of these criticisms

22        concern constraints or community values that would be present at some point

23        along every alternative route. Additionally, there is some opposition to particular

     SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349                                         Petty – Rebuttal
     PUC Docket No. 59475                                             Oncor & LCRA TSC
                                                           Bell County East – Big Hill CCN
                                              -4-
  1           links along Route 894, such as Link J22, due to concerns related to its lack of

 2           paralleling compatible rights of way (ROW) 2 and its alignment along elevated

 3           ridgelines and prominent viewpoints in the Colorado Bend region. 3 Other criticisms

 4           of Route 894 include, among other things, Links F20 and F23, specifically the

 5           purported fall risk due to the occurrence of an EF-3 tornado in the area

 6           approximately four years ago. 4

 7   Q.      HAVE ANY OF THE ARGUMENTS MADE BY INTERVENORS CAUSED YOU

 8           TO CHANGE YOUR RECOMMENDATION OF ROUTE 894?

 9   A.      No. I continue to view Route 894 as the route that best meets the applicable

10           routing factors. But these factors include a broad spectrum of often-competing

11           considerations and may be balanced differently by different parties.                    All 122

12           alternative routes filed with the application satisfy the applicable statutory and

13           regulatory requirements and are acceptable to Applicants. As stated in the rebuttal

14           testimony of Applicants’ witness Ms. Corin Cooley, each of these routes is viable

15           and constructible based on information known at this time.

16                                  II.     REBUTTAL OF NOTICE CONCERNS

17   Q.      SEVERAL INTERVENORS INCLUDING JOHN BURROW (PAGE 2) AND

18           DONNIE JACKSON (PAGE 4) CLAIM THAT THEY DID NOT RECEIVE NOTICE

19           OF THE JUNE 2025 PUBLIC PARTICIPATION MEETINGS.                                     WHY DID

     Ranches, Ltd. at 10:14-19 (May 13, 2026) (Item No. 4271).
     3 See Direct Testimony of John W. Carpenter, III on behalf of Carpenter Land and Cattle Co. at 13:21-

     14:3 (May 13, 2026) (Item No. 4399).
     4 See Direct Testimony of Jason Howton at 25:4-10 (May 12, 2026) (Item No. 3925).

     PUC Docket No. 59475                                                       Oncor & LCRA TSC

  1        APPLICANTS NOT MAIL NOTICE OF THE PUBLIC PARTICIPATION

 2        MEETINGS TO THESE PARTIES?

 3   A.   Applicants did not mail notice of the public participation meetings to John Burrow,

 4        Donnie Jackson, and several others because, at the time, no preliminary route

 5        links were within 520 feet of their properties. After the public participation meetings

 6        were held, Applicants developed and/or modified many route links throughout the

 7        study area in response to feedback received at the public participation meetings,

 8        including adding the preliminary route links affecting these landowners. A detailed

 9        discussion of the route link additions and modifications is contained in Section 6.0

10        of Attachment No. 1 to the Application, the Environmental Assessment and

11        Alternative Route Analysis for the Proposed Bell County East Switch – Big Hill

12        Substation 765 kV Transmission Line Project in Bell, Burnet, Concho, Coryell,

13        Lampasas, Llano, Mason, McCulloch, Menard, Milam, Mills, San Saba, Schleicher,

14        Tom Green, and Williamson Counties, Texas (the “Environmental Assessment and

15        Alternative Route Analysis”).

16   Q.   DID APPLICANTS REVISE THE STUDY AREA BOUNDARY FOR THIS

17        PROJECT AFTER THE PUBLIC PARTICIPATION MEETING IN JUNE 2025?

18   A.   Yes. As stated above, Applicants developed additional route links, in part, as a

19        result of feedback from multiple sources including at the public participation

20        meetings in June 2025. In addition to adding route links and modifying route links

21        throughout the original study area boundary, Applicants expanded the study area

22        boundary to accommodate alternative route links that extended further north into

23        portions of Lampasas, San Saba, and McCulloch counties. This expanded the

     SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349                                          Petty – Rebuttal
     PUC Docket No. 59475                                              Oncor & LCRA TSC
                                                            Bell County East – Big Hill CCN
                                               -6-
  1        study area further north of the preliminary routes links that were presented at the

 2        public participation meetings.

 3   Q.   DID APPLICANTS HOST A PUBLIC PARTICIPATION MEETING FOR THE

 4        LANDOWNERS            AFFECTED     BY    THE    NEW     OR    MODIFIED      ROUTES

 5        MENTIONED ABOVE?

 6   A.   No. Although 16 TAC § 22.52 requires only one public meeting, Applicants hosted

 7        three public meetings across the study area to encourage more engagement and

 8        higher attendance by those affected by the preliminary route links. It is standard

 9        practice that additions or modifications be made to preliminary route links upon

10        interacting with landowners and other agencies at the public meeting and after

11        gathering more data during the data collection process. It is not standard practice

12        to host another public meeting for the landowners newly affected by the additional

13        or modified routes.

14   Q.   DAN KACIR (PAGE 2), DAVID BEHRENS (PAGE 14), MEREDITH MCCALL ON

15        BEHALF OF WALTER AND DEBORAH MCCULLOUGH (PAGE 2), AMANDA

16        RILEY (PAGE 2), AND AARON CRANE (PAGE 2) CLAIM THAT THEY DID NOT

17        RECEIVE NOTICE OF APPLICANTS’ APPLICATION IN THIS DOCKET. DID

18        APPLICANTS MAIL NOTICE OF THEIR APPLICATION TO THESE PARTIES?

19   A.   As I explained in my direct testimony, Applicants were intentionally over-inclusive

20        in their provision of notice, mailing notice to owners of property crossed by or within

21        520 feet of a filed alternative route. Applicants also published notice of their

22        Application in newspapers of general circulation within the counties in the study

23        area.

     SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349                                          Petty – Rebuttal
     PUC Docket No. 59475                                              Oncor & LCRA TSC
                                                            Bell County East – Big Hill CCN
                                               -7-
  1                While I can’t confirm their receipt of the mailed notice, Applicants mailed

 2        notice of its application to Dan Kacir and David Behrens by first-class mail,

 3        consistent with the requirements stated in 16 Texas Administrative Code

 4        § 22.52(a)(4). Applicants attached a copy of the mailing list to its Application as

 5        Attachment No. 12, which includes entries for Dan Kacir and David Behrens at the

 6        PO Box addresses disclosed in their testimonies.

 7                Applicants also published public notice of its Application in 16 newspapers

 8        of general circulation within the counties where facilities are proposed for

 9        construction. Additional information about Applicants’ notice is included in the

10        Affidavit of Jeremy McConnell Attesting to the Provision of Notice to Municipalities,

11        Utilities, Counties, the Department of Defense Siting Clearinghouse, OPUC,

12        TPWD, and Landowners and Newspaper Notice filed in this docket on April 15,

13        2026.

14                With respect to Walter and Deborah McCullough, Applicants did not mail

15        notice of its Application to these intervenors because, as they admit in their direct

16        testimony, these intervenors are not directly affected by the Proposed

17        Transmission Line Project. Rather, they are affected by Applicants’ proposed

18        transmission line project pending under Commission docket number 59182.

19                With respect to Amanda Riley, the address identified in her testimony is

20        listed on the Bell County tax rolls as being owned by Timothy K. and Brenda K.

21        Rivers. Mr. Rivers filed testimony in this proceeding confirming that he owns the

22        property located at the address identified in Ms. Riley’s testimony and he received

  1           notice of the Application on or about April 9, 2026. 5 This is consistent with

 2           Applicants’ list of directly affected landowners filed as Attachment No. 12 to their

 3           Application.

 4                   With respect to Aaron Crane, the address identified in his testimony

 5           corresponds to a parcel with a parcel boundary more than 520 feet from the

 6           centerline at its nearest point. Because he is outside of the notice boundary,

 7           Applicants did not send him direct mail notice.

 8                                III.   REBUTTAL OF ROUTING CONCERNS

 9   Q.      FORMER PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION CHAIRMAN BARRY SMITHERMAN

10           PROVIDED DIRECT TESTIMONY ON BEHALF OF SAVE THE LAMPASAS,

11           CARPENTER LAND & CATTLE CO., LARRY MARTIN, AND THE LINK N3

12           OPPOSITION          LANDOWNERS.             HIS     TESTIMONY      DESCRIBES      THE

13           COMMISSION’S PERSPECTIVE ON ROUTING TRANSMISSION LINES. WHAT

14           IS YOUR RESPONSE?

15   A.      I appreciate the insight and perspective that former Commissioner Mr. Smitherman

16           provides in his direct testimony, as well as his understanding of the Commission’s

17           policy of prudent avoidance. Applicants have made a practice of performing a

18           holistic review and consideration of all the Commission’s routing factors, including

19           a consideration of prudent avoidance, in developing its proposed alternative route

20           links and in offering their opinion in the Application of the route that best meets

21           these factors.



     5 Direct Testimony of Timothy K. Rivers (May 12, 2026) (Item No. 3821).



     SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349                                                   Petty – Rebuttal
     PUC Docket No. 59475                                                       Oncor & LCRA TSC
                                                                     Bell County East – Big Hill CCN
                                                      -9-
  1   Q.     DO YOU DISAGREE WITH ANY CONCLUSIONS THAT MR. SMITHERMAN

 2          HAS MADE REGARDING THE ADEQUACY OF APPLICANTS ROUTES OR

 3          STUDY AREA?

 4   A.     Yes. I strongly disagree with Mr. Smitherman’s conclusion that Applicants have

 5          failed to present to the Commission a set of geographically diverse alternative

 6          transmission line routes that comply with PURA and the Commission’s routing

 7          factors.

 8                  First, Mr. Smitherman’s testimony takes issue with Applicants’ study area,

 9          testifying that “Applicants’ consultants limited the study area to a long narrow

10          straight shot east-west lane.” 6 Importantly, though, the Project’s endpoints dictate

11          the general east-to-west orientation of the study area. The Bell County East Switch

12          and Big Hill Substation are approximately the same latitude, separated by roughly

13          200 miles of primarily east-west distance. Because the endpoints are essentially

14          parallel, any route that deviates significantly to the north or the south must

15          eventually return to the latitude of the destination endpoint in order to reach it.

16          Expanding the north-south orientation of the study area to accommodate routes

17          that swing far north or south, which would necessarily double back toward the

18          center of the corridor, would only add routes that, when compared to other routing

19          options, performed poorly from a length and cost perspective. Additionally,

20          extending farther north would require routing around Fort Hood and other U.S.




     6 Direct Testimony of Barry T. Smitherman on Behalf of Save the Lampasas, Carpenter Land & Cattle

     Co., Larry Martin, and the Link N3 Opposition Landowners at 13:12-15 (May 13, 2026) (Item No. 4334).

     SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349                                                  Petty – Rebuttal
     PUC Docket No. 59475                                                      Oncor & LCRA TSC
                                                                    Bell County East – Big Hill CCN
                                                     - 10 -
  1        Army Corps of Engineer-owned property, which greatly adds to the imprudence of

 2        expanding the study area.

 3                 Mr. Smitherman’s testimony is understandably partial to the concerns of his

 4        clients who do not wish to have a transmission line traverse their property.

 5        However, to conclude that no alternative proposed route should be approved is

 6        particularly obstructionist where, as here, the Applicants have proposed an

 7        uncommonly large slate of routes that span a study area that is 35 miles north-to-

 8        south.

 9                 Second, Mr. Smitherman’s sweeping generalization that this “area of the

10        state . . . has previously been determined to not be well suited to large transmission

11        lines” is at odds with reality. Below is a snapshot taken from Applicants’ Application

12        Attachment No. 10 which depicts the current transmission infrastructure in the area

13        that Mr. Smitherman claims is incompatible with transmission infrastructure:




14

     PUC Docket No. 59475                                              Oncor & LCRA TSC

  1           This map shows only LCRA TSC and Oncor-owned transmission lines. Other

 2           utilities also serve this area of the state and have found viable routes that comply

 3           with the applicable routing criteria.

 4                    Finally, I disagree with his comparison of this Project to the routing from the

 5           Gillespie to Newton 345-kV CREZ Transmission Line Case. 7 In that case, the

 6           application only proposed 11 routes through links that could form at most 27

 7           different forward progressing routes. 8 In this Project, Applicants have proposed

 8           171 alternative route links that can be combined into thousands of potential route

 9           configurations for the Commission’s consideration.

10   Q.      A NUMBER OF INTERVENORS TAKE ISSUE WITH THE CLOSE PROXIMITY

11           OF CERTAIN ALTERNATIVE PROPOSED LINKS AND ROUTES TO

12           HABITABLE STRUCTURES. HOW DO YOU RESPOND?

13   A.      The Commission’s policy of prudent avoidance requires Applicants to limit

14           “exposure to electric and magnetic fields that can be avoided with reasonable

15           investments of money and effort.” Compliance with this policy requires a holistic

16           review of the Commission’s routing factors during the route-selection process.

17           Given the size of the study area and the numerous population centers scattered

18           throughout, including Salado and Lampasas in the eastern half of the study area

19           and Brady and Menard in the western half, Applicants cannot completely avoid

20           locating transmission facilities near habitable structures. Applicants avoided doing

     8 Application of LCRA Transmission Services Corporation to Amend Its Certificate of Convenience and

     Necessity for the Gillespie to Newton 345-kV CREZ Transmission Line in Gillespie, Llano, San Saba,
     Burnet, and Lampasas Counties, Texas, Docket No. 37448, Order at Finding of Fact No. 5 (Apr. 28, 2010).

     SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349                                                  Petty – Rebuttal
     PUC Docket No. 59475                                                      Oncor & LCRA TSC
                                                                    Bell County East – Big Hill CCN
                                                     - 12 -
  1        so where it reasonably could, while considering costs, engineering feasibility, and

 2        the Commission’s routing factors, including ensuring that the routes are reasonably

 3        forward-progressing toward the relevant endpoints.            Ultimately, Applicants

 4        provided a geographically diverse range of routing options that avoided schools

 5        and other habitable structures, parks, and recreational areas where practicable.

 6   Q.   SEVERAL INTERVENORS INCLUDING FRANK ELLETT ON BEHALF OF

 7        LEAH MEYER, ANDY MEYER, AND G6 LANDOWNERS LEGAL FUND, LLC

 8        (PAGE 12), AND ALBERT HOWARD BROAD III (PAGE 20), TESTIFIED THAT

 9        THE LINKS BISECT THEIR PROPERTY RATHER THAN PARALLEL

10        PROPERTY BOUNDARIES AND/OR EXISTING COMPATIBLE RIGHTS-OF-

11        WAY. HOW DO YOU RESPOND?

12   A.   While Applicants try to route along apparent property boundaries obtained from

13        county tax and/or appraisal district records and existing compatible corridors when

14        reasonably able, it is not always feasible to do so. This highlights the need to

15        balance existing constraints and the Commission’s routing factors across a large

16        study area. Property lines cannot reasonably be followed for the entire length of a

17        route due to cost considerations and general engineering constraints. Property

18        boundaries are often irregular, so paralleling them for extended distances would

19        require a large number of turning structures, increasing project costs. For this

20        Project in particular, due to its length, paralleling apparent property boundaries for

21        the entire length of a route would increase costs and construction timelines

22        exponentially.

     PUC Docket No. 59475                                              Oncor & LCRA TSC
                                                            Bell County East – Big Hill CCN
                                              - 13 -
  1   Q.   MANY INTERVENORS SUCH AS FREDERICK BARTLETT WULFF, SR. (PAGE

 2        14), KEVIN NEWMAN ON BEHALF OF NEWMAN SURFACE PROPERTIES, LP

 3        (PAGE 10), AND SHERRI FISCHER (PAGE 3) HAVE TESTIFIED THAT THE

 4        PROJECT WOULD HAVE A NEGATIVE IMPACT ON THEIR ENJOYMENT OF

 5        THE RECREATIONAL ASPECTS OF THEIR PROPERTY AS IT RELATES TO

 6        THE NATURAL ENVIRONMENT AND WILDLIFE ON THEIR LAND. HOW DO

 7        YOU RESPOND?

 8   A.   Impacts to wildlife and environmental concerns are addressed more fully in the

 9        direct and rebuttal testimonies of Mr. Russell Marusak, as well as the

10        Environmental Assessment and Alternative Route Analysis filed as Attachment

11        No. 1 to Applicants’ Application. However, it is Applicants’ experience that the

12        presence of a transmission line on a property does not have a material adverse

13        effect on recreational activities or enjoyment of the land, generally. Thousands of

14        miles of transmission lines exist today across properties that are primarily used for

15        recreational activities.

16   Q.   SEVERAL INTERVENORS, INCLUDING MARY ALEXANDER ON BEHALF OF

17        SOLANA DEVELOPMENT LP, SOLANA RANCH COMPANY, AND DMB

18        DEVELOPMENT LLC (PAGE 7), SCOTT KIELLA ON BEHALF OF BOHKERS,

19        LLC – SERIES 119 AND KIELLA LAND INVESTMENTS, LTD. (PAGE 8), AND

20        BRUCE WHITIS ON BEHALF OF WHITIS LAND INVESTMENTS, LP (PAGE 8)

21        HAVE FILED DIRECT TESTIMONY GENERALLY CLAIMING THAT THE

22        PROJECT WILL HARM CERTAIN PLANNED OR FUTURE RESIDENTIAL AND

23        COMMERCIAL PROPERTY DEVELOPMENTS. THESE INTERVENORS ALSO

     SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349                                         Petty – Rebuttal
     PUC Docket No. 59475                                             Oncor & LCRA TSC
                                                           Bell County East – Big Hill CCN
                                              - 14 -
  1        CLAIM THAT CERTAIN ROUTES WILL RESULT IN THE HARM OR

 2        DESTRUCTION OF USABILITY AND HABITABILITY OF SECTIONS OF

 3        PROPERTY. HOW DO YOU RESPOND?

 4   A.   There are countless examples across Applicants’ service areas where residential

 5        and commercial areas have developed immediately adjacent to transmission line

 6        ROW. In my experience, future development plans commonly change, making

 7        them far more flexible.

 8              Also, it is my understanding that the Commission has historically been

 9        reluctant to consider future development and has not afforded proposed future

10        development the same consideration as existing constraints, as explained in the

11        Order on Rehearing in Docket No. 45866 (pages 7-8).           Nevertheless, the

12        Commission is free to take into consideration the stage of any current

13        development, the amount of resources already committed to the development, or

14        the impact that the Proposed Transmission Line Project may have on the

15        development. If the Commission ultimately selects a route that crosses parcels in

16        some stage of development planning, the Project may impact more habitable

17        structures than are counted in Applicants’ CCN Application or may have additional

18        impacts on land use. This does not render these routes non-viable.

19   Q.   SEVERAL INTERVENORS INCLUDING WENDY AND SHIRLEY FLEMING

20        (PAGE 9) HAVE DISCUSSED OIL AND GAS AND OTHER DRILLING

21        FACILITIES THAT MAY BE IMPACTED BY THE ROUTES FILED IN THE

22        APPLICATION. HOW DO APPLICANTS RESPOND TO SUCH COMMENTS?



     SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349                                       Petty – Rebuttal
     PUC Docket No. 59475                                           Oncor & LCRA TSC
                                                         Bell County East – Big Hill CCN
                                            - 15 -
  1   A.   Applicants sought to route the Proposed Transmission Line Project to avoid active

 2        well sites, identifying existing constraints through data collection activities such as

 3        aerial imagery, field reconnaissance, and publicly available well data provided by

 4        the Railroad Commission of Texas.             However, ongoing oil and gas-related

 5        development, including mining of sand to use for fracking, is present throughout

 6        Texas. It is likely that all of the filed routes will be impacted to some degree by

 7        such development, even though the precise impacts would vary from route to

 8        route.   Applicants have substantial experience with, and a longstanding

 9        commitment to, working with affected oil and gas companies, mining companies,

10        and surface estate owners and will work to resolve routing issues that may arise

11        from such development.

12   Q.   BRUCE MATHIS ON BEHALF OF BRIGGS ESTATES HOA AND SAVE THE

13        LAMPASAS (PAGE 10) TESTIFIES THAT FIGURE 3-1 IN APPENDIX G OF THE

14        ENVIRONMENTAL ASSESSMENT AND ROUTING STUDY FAILS TO SHOW

15        CERTAIN HABITABLE STRUCTURES ON THEIR PROPERTIES. WHAT IS

16        YOUR RESPONSE TO THESE INTERVENORS AND OTHER INTERVENORS

17        REGARDING FEATURES NOT DEPICTED ON THE CONSTRAINTS MAP?

18   A.   Applicants underwent extensive efforts, including the review of aerial imagery, use

19        of publicly available records, field reconnaissance, and solicitation of landowner

20        feedback at multiple public participation meetings to obtain all information

21        necessary to make Figure 3-1 as accurate as practicable.             With respect to

22        identifying habitable structures on Figure 3-1, Applicants only marked habitable

23        structures within 520 feet of the centerline of the proposed alternative route links.

 5        impact routing for the final approved route, Applicants will cooperate with directly
